Information received since the November meeting points to continued labor-market strength and solid economic activity, with inflation still below 2 percent. A forward-looking Phillips curve and simple policy rules support the Committee’s gradual approach to rate increases, while the Orphanides real-time measurement critique and evidence that tightening can damp future consumption argue for caution. Incorporating the FSR lens, elevated valuation pressures and rising nonfinancial business leverage alongside generally resilient household balance sheets, well-capitalized banks, and limited short-term funding risks suggest overall vulnerabilities are moderate but skewed by risk appetite. This mix supports gradualism but tempers the otherwise positive tone, especially given symmetric 2 percent inflation aims and close monitoring of inflation dynamics. Net assessment: moderately positive, with added caution due to valuation and leverage vulnerabilities.
